record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the smallest possible maximum degree of a plane spanner that is required to be a subgraph of the standard Euclidean Delaunay triangulation of the input point set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13. What is the smallest maximum degree that can be achieved for plane spanners that are subgraphs of the standard Delaunay triangulation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in general position in the Euclidean plane, and let DT(P) denote its (standard) Euclidean Delaunay triangulation: the straight-line plane graph in which two points p, q ∈ P are joined by an edge if and only if there exists a closed disk that has p and q on its boundary and contains no other point of P in its interior.

For a real number t ≥ 1, a geometric graph G on the vertex set P (with straight-line edges weighted by Euclidean distance) is called a t-spanner of P if for every pair of points p, q ∈ P, the length of a shortest path from p to q in G is at most t · |pq|, where |pq| denotes the Euclidean distance. The graph G is called plane if its edges do not cross.

Define
   d* := inf { Δ : there exists a constant t ≥ 1 such that, for every finite point set P in general position in the plane, there is a plane t-spanner of P that is a subgraph of DT(P) and has maximum vertex degree at most Δ }.

Determine the exact value of d*.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known upper bound is maximum degree 7, achieved by Bonichon, Gavoille, Hanusse and Ilcinkas (2010), giving a plane constant-spanner that is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation with max degree 7. No matching lower bound is known; if one requires the spanner to be a subgraph of DT(P), the optimal maximum degree remains undetermined. Subsequent works that achieve smaller degree (6, 4, …) drop the subgraph-of-Delaunay requirement. The problem appears to still be open as of the most recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Bounded Degree Planar Geometric Spanners (arXiv:1003.4963)
status_evidence.snippet: A subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation with maximum degree 7 can be computed that is a strong plane t-spanner.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound for plane spanner that is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation is maximum degree 7.

status_evidence.title: On plane geometric spanners: A survey and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on plane geometric t-spanners, including bounded-degree subgraphs of the Delaunay triangulation.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of the smallest achievable maximum degree for a plane spanner that is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Degree Four Plane Spanners: Simpler and Better
status_evidence.snippet: Plane spanner with maximum degree 4 of the complete Euclidean graph (not required to be subgraph of DT).
status_evidence.claim: Improvements below degree 7 in the literature do not maintain the subgraph-of-Delaunay constraint.
